<Aside type="note">
  Script Composer is **not** part of `@aptos-labs/ts-sdk`. It was removed from
  the TypeScript SDK so that applications which do not use it no longer have to
  bundle its WASM binary (see
  [aptos-labs/aptos-ts-sdk#688](https://github.com/aptos-labs/aptos-ts-sdk/issues/688)).
  It is now published as the standalone
  [`@aptos-labs/script-composer-sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@aptos-labs/script-composer-sdk)
  package, developed in the
  [aptos-labs/script-composer-sdk](https://github.com/aptos-labs/script-composer-sdk)
  repository. If you were using Script Composer through an older `ts-sdk`
  release (last included in `1.39.0`), install the standalone package and
  update your imports as described below — the composer API itself is
  unchanged.
</Aside>

## Overview

In the basic API, you can only specify one entry function call for a single transaction. Advanced builders might want to invoke multiple **public** Move functions in one transaction. Script Composer enables this: you describe a sequence of calls with `addBatchedCalls`, pass return values from one call into the next, and the SDK compiles them into a single script transaction.

## Installation

Install the standalone package together with its `@aptos-labs/ts-sdk` and WASM (`@aptos-labs/script-composer-pack`) peer dependencies:

<PackageTabs type="add" pkg="@aptos-labs/script-composer-sdk @aptos-labs/script-composer-pack @aptos-labs/ts-sdk" pkgManagers={['npm', 'yarn', 'pnpm']} />

Browser applications also need the `buffer` package and a global `Buffer` polyfill before importing the SDK:

```typescript
import { Buffer } from "buffer";

(window as typeof window & { Buffer: typeof Buffer }).Buffer = Buffer;
```

## Basic Usage

Import `BuildScriptComposerTransaction` and `CallArgument` from `@aptos-labs/script-composer-sdk` — not from `@aptos-labs/ts-sdk`:

```typescript filename="example.ts"
import { Aptos, AptosConfig, Network } from "@aptos-labs/ts-sdk";
import {
  BuildScriptComposerTransaction,
  CallArgument,
} from "@aptos-labs/script-composer-sdk";

const aptosConfig = new AptosConfig({ network: Network.TESTNET });
// Replace with the sender's account address.
const sender = "0x1";

const tx = await BuildScriptComposerTransaction({
  sender,
  // Building a composed transaction reads on-chain state (module ABIs and
  // bytecode), so it needs an AptosConfig for the target network.
  aptosConfig,
  builder: async (composer) => {
    // Withdraw some Coin.
    const coin = await composer.addBatchedCalls({
      function: "0x1::coin::withdraw",
      functionArguments: [CallArgument.newSigner(0), 1],
      typeArguments: ["0x1::aptos_coin::AptosCoin"],
    });

    // Convert the coin into a fungible asset. coin[0] is the first return
    // value of the first call added above.
    const fungibleAsset = await composer.addBatchedCalls({
      function: "0x1::coin::coin_to_fungible_asset",
      functionArguments: [coin[0]],
      typeArguments: ["0x1::aptos_coin::AptosCoin"],
    });

    // Deposit the fungible asset returned by the second call.
    await composer.addBatchedCalls({
      function: "0x1::primary_fungible_store::deposit",
      functionArguments: [sender, fungibleAsset[0]],
      typeArguments: [],
    });
    return composer;
  },
});
```

> Please note that the current example is only for reference on how to use Script Composer to combine transactions, receive return values from public functions, and pass them to the next function.

For transactions that need secondary signers and/or a fee payer, use `BuildScriptComposerMultiAgentTransaction` from the same package instead. For a sponsored single-signer transaction, pass `withFeePayer: true` to `BuildScriptComposerTransaction`.

## Transaction Processing

After combining the transaction, we can use interfaces like sign transaction / simulate transaction / submit transaction from `@aptos-labs/ts-sdk`:

We'll use the simulate transaction interface to show how to use it:

```typescript filename="example.ts"
const aptos = new Aptos(aptosConfig);

const [simulateResult] = await aptos.transaction.simulate.simple({
  transaction: tx,
});

console.log("simulate_result: ", simulateResult);
```

## Technical Principles

Under the hood, the SDK will invoke a WASM binary (provided by `@aptos-labs/script-composer-pack`) to compile the series of Move calls into a `CompiledScript`. This will guarantee that the type and ability safety of Move is still being honored during the construction process. For the SDK users, this means:

1. Ability safety:
   a. If the returned value does not have the Drop ability, the returned value needs to be consumed by subsequent calls.
   b. If the returned value does not have the Copy ability, the returned value can only be passed to subsequent calls once.
2. The caller will need to make sure they pass the right values as arguments to subsequent calls. In the previous example, the `0x1::coin::coin_to_fungible_asset` function will expect an argument of `Coin<AptosCoin>`.

This implements [AIP-102](https://github.com/aptos-foundation/AIPs/blob/main/aips/aip-102.md)
